sections.h2: Who bills and who values property tax in Stark County, Ohio?
sections.html:
Two elected offices split the work. The Stark County Auditor values every parcel and runs the exemption programs, and the Stark County Treasurer sends the bills and takes payment. Both are in Canton and both post weekday hours of 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., closed on government holidays.

The county seat is Canton, and the 374,853 residents counted in 2020 make Stark the eighth most populous county in Ohio. Its parcels fall into seventeen public school districts, from Canton City and Massillon City to Plain Local and Tuslaw Local, and the Treasurer's FAQ says most property tax dollars go to the schools in the owner's district. A tax rate table for each district is available in print at the Treasurer's office.

sections.h2: When are Stark County property taxes due, and what if I miss the date?
sections.html:
Stark County bills twice a year. The Treasurer's FAQ says bills are mailed in January for payment in February, and again in June for payment in July. The due date is published in the Canton Repository about ten days beforehand, and it can move: in 2026 the Treasurer's site described delays tied to House Bill 186 that pushed back the autopay letters from September to October.

The rules on lateness are blunt:

  • A bill is late the day after the due date, and there are no individual extensions.
  • A U.S. Postal Service postmark counts as the date of payment, but a private postage meter does not, and a check dated after the due date is late.
  • The FAQ says a ten percent penalty is added to current taxes that are late, with interest accruing on balances that stay unpaid a full year.
  • Not receiving a bill is no excuse. You can print a copy from the Treasurer's site, visit the office, or ask for an email copy at 330-451-7814.

If a mortgage servicer pays your taxes from escrow, the servicer gets the bill twice a year and you receive a courtesy copy each January. After a refinance, the lender must ask in writing to correct the mailing address.

sections.h2: What happens in Stark County when taxes stay unpaid?
sections.html:
Delinquent parcels can be pulled into either of two enforcement paths, according to the Treasurer's FAQ. One is a tax lien certificate sale, where title does not transfer but the buyer of the certificate may file for foreclosure if the lien goes unpaid. The other is a tax foreclosure filed with the Prosecutor's office, ending in a Sheriff's sale, where title does change hands. The Treasurer's site announced a 2026 tax lien sale, with payment in full required to come off the list, certified funds only, and a $200 tax lien fee at redemption.

Foreclosure follows a set timeline, as the Treasurer's delinquent tax page lays it out. A summons goes out by certified mail once the complaint is filed with the Clerk of Courts, and the owner has 28 days to respond. An order of sale then goes to the Sheriff, and the newspaper advertises the sale three consecutive weeks before it happens. The owner can redeem any time before the court confirms the sale by paying all taxes, assessments, penalties, interest, fees and court costs in certified funds.

For a seller, that means delinquent tax is a deadline with a known endpoint. Selling before the confirmation entry lets the proceeds clear the lien instead of losing the house at auction.

sections.h2: Can I pay back Stark County taxes in installments?
sections.html:
A payment plan exists for back taxes, though not for the current bill. The Treasurer's delinquent tax page sets these terms:

  • Only the titled owner, or a documented agent, may sign the contract.
  • The delinquent balance must be $1,000 or more. Balances from $1,000 to $1,999 get a 12-month plan, and $2,000 or more gets 24 months.
  • A 20 percent down payment is due at signing, along with the current half's tax balance.
  • Installments are due on the 20th of each month.
  • A prior defaulted contract rules out a new one.

The current year's tax must still be paid in full by each due date, and the office says it cannot extend a due date or set up a plan for current-year taxes. Miss any payment and the contract defaults. A contract, unlike a payoff, is an extra obligation to explain to a buyer, so most sellers clear the balance at closing instead.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Stark County property value?
sections.html:
File a complaint with the Auditor for the Board of Revision. ORC 5715.19 sets the deadline at March 31 of the year after the tax year in question, or the close of first-half collection if that is later, and a mailed complaint counts by its U.S. postmark. The board must decide within 180 days of the filing deadline. Pay what you can while the complaint is open: the statute lets the Treasurer accept the amount computed on your claimed value.

A second complaint on the same parcel in the same update period is barred unless the property sold at arm's length, lost value to a casualty, gained a substantial improvement, or saw occupancy change by 15 percent or more. The Ohio Department of Taxation describes a full reappraisal every six years with a value update every three, and it suggests asking the county Auditor, at 330-451-7085 for Stark, whether an informal review is offered first.

sections.h2: What tax relief is available to Stark County homeowners?
sections.html:
The Auditor's relief page groups four programs: homestead and owner occupancy, the Board of Revision complaint, CAUV for working farmland, and special exemption or assessment matters. State rules for the first one are posted by the Ohio Department of Taxation. For tax year 2026 it lists a reduction of $29,700 of market value for low-income seniors and disabled owners and $59,400 for disabled veterans, and an income threshold of $41,000 for the first group. Homestead applications are due by December 31 of the year they are sought.

A denied application can be appealed to the Board of Revision on form DTE 106B within 60 days of the denial notice. House Bill 96 of 2025 also lets county commissioners add a local-option homestead exemption. Whether Stark County has adopted one is a question for the Homestead department at 330-451-7323.

sections.h2: How do property taxes work in a Stark County sale?
sections.html:
The title company asks the Treasurer for the current balance, and the seller settles any unpaid half from the sale. On the transfer side, the Stark County Auditor charges a conveyance fee printed as $.004 of the price, rounded up to the next $100, plus $.50 for each tax parcel, payable by check or cash. A transfer cannot be recorded until the Auditor stamps the deed.

A buyer comparing houses can look up any parcel's tax history on the Treasurer's site, which offers real estate search, prior year search, the delinquent taxpayer list and a Sheriff sales page. Sellers who have fallen behind can read the posted list of delinquent parcels, last published as of May 1, 2026, and call the Treasurer to confirm a payoff before a closing is set.

faqs.q: What is the penalty for paying Stark County property tax late?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's FAQ says a ten percent penalty is added to late current taxes, and interest builds if a balance stays unpaid for a full year. There are no individual extensions, and a bill is late the day after its due date.

faqs.q: When do Stark County property tax bills go out?
faqs.a: In January for the February payment and in June for the July payment. The Treasurer's FAQ says the due date is published in the Canton Repository about ten days before it falls, and some years the dates shift.

faqs.q: Can I set up a payment plan for Stark County back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, if you are the titled owner with a delinquent balance of at least $1,000 and no prior defaulted plan. A 20 percent down payment and the current half are due at signing, with monthly installments on the 20th. Current-year taxes cannot be put on a plan.

faqs.q: Where do I file a Stark County property value complaint?
faqs.a: With the Stark County Auditor, which presents it to the Board of Revision. Call 330-451-7998 or 330-451-7949. The filing window under Ohio law closes March 31 of the following year, or the close of first-half collection if later.

faqs.q: Does a Stark County tax foreclosure take my house right away?
faqs.a: No. The Treasurer's page describes a filed complaint, a 28-day response period for the owner, an order of sale, a Sheriff's sale advertised three weeks, and a right to redeem before the court confirms the sale. Redemption takes full payment in certified funds.
